subject: arcadeCabinet

Category: Object.
Subject: 1980s arcade cabinet.
Style: synthwave.

spec.name: Neon Drive '84 Arcade Cabinet
spec.description: A 1980s upright arcade cabinet in synthwave style: a near-black purple body with magenta and cyan neon T-molding, a glowing retro-sunset screen, a backlit NEON DRIVE marquee, a two-player control deck, and perspective-grid, striped-sun and mountain side art.
spec.layout: STATIC model, no joints. Real arcade scale. Axes: +Y up, front faces +Z, left side is +X, centred on x = 0. The cabinet side panel is the signature silhouette. Its z-y outline from the lowest point, going up the front and back down: kick plinth z -0.44..0.34, y 0..0.10 (recessed). Lower body front face at z 0.44 from y 0.10 to 0.86. Control deck wedge from z 0.30 to 0.52, y 0.86..1.06: its sloped top plane runs from (z 0.30, y 1.06) down to the front lip (z 0.52, y 0.98), and the lip front face drops from y 0.98 to 0.86 at z 0.52. Above the deck sits the monitor housing. Its front is the bezel plane, tilted back about 13 degrees from (z 0.30, y 1.06) up to (z 0.20, y 1.50); the bezel normal in z-y is about (0.975, 0.222). The marquee box sits on top, y 1.50..1.80, from z -0.44 to a vertical front face at z 0.26. It overhangs the bezel top by 0.06. The back is a flat plane at z -0.44 from y 0 to 1.80. Side panels are 0.03 thick: outer faces at x = +-0.35, inner faces at x = +-0.32. Neon T-molding tubes sit at x = +-0.356 so the overall width is 0.72. Vertical order, bottom to top: plinth, coin door and lower cabinet, control deck, CRT bezel and screen, glowing marquee. SYNTHWAVE STYLE: the body is near-black purple (cabBlack and cabNavy). Everything that glows is neon magenta, cyan, pink, violet or sunset orange and yellow, built as small flat-colour parts seated on the surface and wrapped in glow() from the glow kit (neon trim, coin slots, lit buttons, screen, marquee sign). Chrome and steel only for hardware. Side art, built by one part and seen on both x sides: a magenta perspective grid floor on the lower body with its horizon line at y 0.86, a big striped orange-to-yellow sun rising over the horizon on the monitor-housing side, and a cyan wireframe mountain ridge with stars on the marquee side. The title is NEON DRIVE; the screen shows a 1984 outrun scene (striped sun, grid road, mountains, a tiny cyan car, HI-SCORE text). Every part uses only the palette colours; stripes, seams, rivets and emblems are separate small parts.

parts.builds: Everything from the floor to y 0.86 except the side art and the T-molding: recessed black kick plinth (z -0.44..0.34, y 0..0.10) with a thin neonMagenta underglow strip on its front face. Lower cabinet carcass: two side panels in cabBlack (x +-0.32..0.35, z -0.44..0.44, y 0.10..0.86, side outline as in the layout), front panel at z 0.44, back panel with a recessed rear service door (darkSteel with a chrome lock, hinge pins, a slotted vent grille of about 8 slits, a power-cord entry with a black cord looping down, a small fan-vent circle and a warning-sticker rectangle in sunYellow). Front coin door built at the coinDoor mount: a darkSteel plate (x +-0.17, y 0.38..0.70) with two chrome coin-mech boxes, each with a glowing coinGlow slot, a coin-return flap with a dark recess, a small cyan 'COIN' label strip, a chrome lock, four chrome rivets and a thin coinGlow-lit rim. Above the door, a lit 'INSERT COIN' sign made of a black plate with a glowing neonPink bar. Below it, a cabNavy panel with a small neonViolet vent grille. A narrow cash-box flap line, and two lit square coin buttons in neonCyan at either side of the door. The top surface of the body is closed at y 0.86 (cabNavy), covered by the control deck above.
parts.attaches: Rests on y = 0. Its top plane at y 0.86 (mount bodyTop) is where controlDeck (z 0.30..0.52) and screenAssembly (z -0.44..0.30) start. Its outer side faces at x = +-0.35 are covered by sideArtAndTrim, which does not touch the carcass shapes.

parts.builds: The control deck wedge, z 0.30..0.52, y 0.86..1.06. Two side cheeks (panels x +-0.32..0.35, outline (z,y): (0.30,0.86),(0.52,0.86),(0.52,0.98),(0.30,1.06)) in cabBlack. A sloped panelPurple control plate between the cheeks, from deckBack down to deckFront at about a 20 degree slope, with a chrome front lip bar and a woodDark underlip. Decor on the plate: a cabNavy inset overlay with a neonMagenta grid, a cyan chevron and star decals, and a sunset stripe set built from thin sunOrange / neonPink / neonViolet strips along the front. Controls, mirrored about x = 0. Player 1 is at -X and player 2 at +X from the player's view. Joysticks at x = +-0.26, z 0.40: a darkSteel round base plate, a chrome rod, a dust-washer disc and a big glossy ball top, neonMagenta for P1 and neonCyan for P2. Three fire buttons per player at x = +-0.16, +-0.11, +-0.06, each a short rubber base ring and a glossy dome cap in buttonRed, buttonYellow and buttonBlue (P1) and buttonGreen, buttonYellow and buttonRed (P2) with a small white highlight dot. Two small start buttons at x = +-0.03, z 0.34, glowing neonPink and neonCyan, with tiny '1P'/'2P' label plates. Small numbered label strips in white beside each cluster. A glowing neonMagenta edge line along the back of the plate where it meets the bezel. All lit buttons and neon pieces are wrapped in glow().
parts.attaches: Sits on bodyTop (y 0.86) at z 0.30..0.52. The back edge (mount deckBack, y 1.06, z 0.30) meets the bezelBottom of screenAssembly. The cheek outer faces are at x = +-0.35, flush with the side panels.

parts.builds: The monitor housing above bodyTop behind the deck (z -0.44..0.30, y 0.86..1.06) and the tilted bezel up to y 1.50. Two side panels in cabBlack (x +-0.32..0.35) with the outline (z,y): (-0.44,0.86),(0.30,0.86),(0.30,1.06),(0.20,1.50),(-0.44,1.50). A back panel at z -0.44 (y 0.86..1.50) with a slotted vent grille (8 slits). A front fascia under the bezel (z 0.28..0.30, y 0.86..1.06), cabNavy, with a chrome speaker grille made of 6 slits and a small neonCyan power LED. The bezel is a black tilted frame on the plane through (z 0.30, y 1.06) and (z 0.20, y 1.50), in cabBlack with an inner screenGlass surround. Neon swoosh stripes in neonMagenta, neonViolet and neonCyan run diagonally across the bezel corners, thin separate parts. The CRT glass is a slightly curved flat plane (x +-0.26, y 1.12..1.44, along the bezel plane at screenCenter) carrying an svg() texture of the outrun scene wrapped in glow(): a purple-to-pink sky gradient, a striped sunOrange-to-sunYellow sun, a cyan wireframe mountain ridge, a magenta perspective-grid road, a tiny cyan car, a 'HI-SCORE 084000' text line and an '1UP' label. Over it, thin horizontal scanline strips in a slightly darker tone, a diagonal white glass-reflection streak at low opacity, and a rounded chrome-trimmed rubber gasket frame around the glass. A top glowing neonMagenta line where the bezel meets the marquee at bezelTop. Sun and side art on the outer side faces belong to sideArtAndTrim.
parts.attaches: Starts on bodyTop at y 0.86 for z < 0.30. Meets controlDeck at bezelBottom (z 0.30, y 1.06) and the marquee at bezelTop and marqueeBottom (y 1.50). Outer side faces at x = +-0.35.

parts.builds: The topper box, y 1.50..1.80, z -0.44..0.26, x +-0.35. Two side panels in cabBlack with a slight top bevel, a back panel, a top cap in cabNavy with a thin chrome rim and a row of small slotted vents. A chrome-trimmed frame at the front face (z 0.26) surrounds a backlit sign plane (x +-0.29, y 1.54..1.78) carrying an svg() texture wrapped in glow(): the title NEON DRIVE in chunky chrome-gradient italic letters with neonMagenta and neonCyan outlines, a striped sun disc behind the text, a thin neon horizon grid under it and a small 'ROUND 1' badge and '1984' stamp. Under the sign, a thin neonMagenta tube along the frame bottom (y 1.52) and a neonCyan tube along the top edge (y 1.78), both wrapped in glow(). Small sunYellow star sparks beside the title, a few chrome screws at the frame corners, and a tiny neonPink light bar on top of the cap. The underside of the overhang (y 1.50, z 0.20..0.26) is a black strip. Side art on the outer side faces is built by sideArtAndTrim.
parts.attaches: Sits on screenAssembly at y 1.50 (mount marqueeBottom). Its front face at z 0.26 overhangs the bezelTop at z 0.20. Its top (marqueeTop, y 1.80) is the model's highest point. Outer side faces are at x = +-0.35.

parts.builds: All decoration that lies on the outside of the cabinet, mirrored on both sides (x = +-0.352..0.357, thin extruded or slab parts about 0.004 thick, seated on the side panel outer faces at x = +-0.35). T-molding: round neonMagenta tubes (radius about 0.006, each wrapped in glow()) at x = +-0.356 following the outer edge of each side panel outline: front edge of the lower body (z 0.44, y 0.10..0.86), the deck wedge outline, the bezel slope, the marquee front and top edge, and the back edge (z -0.44), with a cyan accent tube following the lower plinth edge and the marquee outline. Short corner joints at each bend. Side art, per side: (1) lower body (y 0.12..0.84): a cabNavy background panel with a neonMagenta perspective grid floor, built from horizontal lines getting closer toward the horizon at y 0.86 and converging diagonals fanning toward a vanishing point at about (z -0.05, y 0.86), and a bright neonCyan horizon line at y 0.85. (2) monitor-housing side (y 0.88..1.48): a big semicircular sun, centre (z -0.10, y 1.0), radius 0.30, made of stacked sunYellow, sunOrange and neonPink horizontal bands with growing dark gaps toward the bottom, and rising from the horizon. A neonViolet silhouette mountain range of 3-4 extruded peaks at its base, and a thin neonCyan outline arc around the sun. (3) marquee side (y 1.52..1.78): a cabBlack background with 8-10 small star sparkles in white, neonPink and neonCyan, a cyan wireframe mountain zigzag line and a magenta chevron stripe. A small chrome 'NEON DRIVE' badge plate with a neonCyan underline at the sun's right on the lower body (z -0.30, y 0.7). Rear: nothing.
parts.attaches: Everything sits on the outer side faces x = +-0.35 of lowerBody, controlDeck, screenAssembly and marquee, following the side outline in the layout. It adds no geometry inside the cabinet.

calls.reasoning:
I'm settling on a static model with no joints, so the spec's joints list stays empty, with the joystick and buttons left as plain props if they show up at all. For the size I'm going with a classic upright cabinet footprint, around 0.78 wide, 1.85 tall, and 0.95 deep.

I'm laying out the cabinet's side profile now: a recessed kick plinth at the bottom, a lower body with a coin door, an angled control panel sticking out front, and a tilted bezel above with the marquee on top. I'm also sizing the side panels and working out where the shell parts meet so they don't overlap.

I'm now breaking the cabinet into four parts: a lower body from floor to about 0.88 with the plinth, coin door, and side art, a control deck around 0.88 to 1.06 holding the joysticks and buttons, an upper screen housing with the bezel and synthwave CRT scene, and a marquee topper reaching about 1.82 with the backlit title sign.

I'm working through how the side panels divide between the parts: the lower body takes the sides down to about 0.88, the upper screen housing covers the tilted section up to 1.52, and the marquee takes the top. I'm also deciding how the side art stays continuous, with a magenta perspective grid on the lower sides and a striped sun rising above the horizon on the upper ones.

I'm now defining the side panel profile in the spec so every part can share it: a thin panel about 0.03 thick, with the outer edge at about ±0.36 across for the T-molding.

I'm sketching the side profile point by point: the back bottom, then a kick recess at the front where the plinth steps in, with the lower body's front face running up to about 0.86. The control deck sits above that and overhangs forward, and the monitor bezel begins tilting back from around 1.04.

I'm finishing the front profile of the marquee and bezel: the bezel tilts back from about z 0.32 at the bottom to 0.18 at the top, and the marquee's front stays roughly vertical at z 0.24. I'm also checking the rear, which runs straight up at z -0.46.

I'm deciding the back should be a single straight plane at z -0.44 instead of stepping, which gives an overall depth of 0.96 and a height of 1.80, so the size comes out to [0.72, 1.80, 0.96].

I'm sketching the side panel outline point by point, with the lower body's sides running up to about 0.86. For the control deck I'm considering a wedge-shaped side cheek whose top slopes forward and down, so it can overhang the body.

I'm working out the control deck's shape: a wedge sitting between about 0.86 and 1.06 in height, with its top sloping down toward the front and the overhang reaching out past the body.

I'm checking how the control deck box sits against the screen housing: the deck spans z 0.20 to 0.52 at heights 0.86 to 1.06, while the housing's lower part stays behind z 0.20 so the two only meet and don't overlap.

I'm checking the marquee's footprint and how its front sits over the bezel, which leaves a small overhang. For the side panel of the screen housing, I'm laying out an outline from the lower edge up to the bezel's tilt, and I'm still working out the exact point where that front edge meets the top.

I'm pinning down the housing's side outline: it runs flat along the bottom, steps forward to the bezel, then slopes back up to the top edge.

I'm fixing the deck's box between z 0.30 and 0.52 so it sits right against the housing's lower section, and I'm checking that the control panel's sloped top ends at the bezel's bottom edge. The bezel's tilt runs from about (0.30, 1.06) up to (0.20, 1.50), so I'm estimating the glass plane inside it from roughly (0.28, 1.10) to (0.215, 1.46).

I'm working out the screen opening's inset and the bezel's surface normal, then placing the marquee sign's front and span.

I'm listing the mount points for the cabinet parts next: the deck's back and front, the body top, the bezel's bottom and top, the screen centre, and the marquee's bottom and front, along with the coin door and the side panel offset.

I'm listing the five parts now, starting with the lower body on the floor: plinth, side panels up to 0.86, a front panel with a coin door, and a rear with vents. Then the control deck, with two joysticks, six coloured buttons, lit start buttons, and purple-black decals.

I'm now setting out the five parts for the cabinet: the lower body with its plinth, side panels, coin door, and rear vents, then the control deck with its joysticks, buttons, and decals. The screen assembly comes next, with the bezel, CRT glass, and side sun art, followed by the marquee with its backlit title sign and neon edges.

I'm settling on a fifth part, a side-art-and-trim piece that covers the full height of both sides with the T-molding, sun, grid, and mountain decals. Its box runs the full depth at the sides, with the art starting around y 0.12 above the plinth, and the decals sit on the panel surface at x about 0.352.

I'm setting the palette now: a deep purple-black and navy for the cabinet, panel purple, and neon magenta, cyan, pink, violet, plus orange and yellow for the sun.

Now I'm listing the palette: a deep purple-black and navy for the cabinet, steel and chrome trim, a dark steel for the mechanical bits, and neon accents in red, yellow, blue, and green for the buttons.

I'm settling the spec details now: the coin door plate sits on the front face between about 0.38 and 0.70 in height, the lower front runs from 0.10 to 0.86, and the kick plate steps back to z 0.34. The control deck's side cheeks are a wedge from z 0.30 to 0.52, sloping from 0.86 up to 1.06.

I'm working out which side the player-one joystick goes on, sorting out whether the cabinet's left and right are the viewer's or the player's.

I'm working out where player one's joystick goes: since a player facing the cabinet has their right toward +X, player one sits at about x -0.17 with player two mirrored at +0.17, and the start buttons go near the centre. Each side gets three buttons spaced outward from its joystick.

I'm working out the control panel's layout now: two joysticks sitting symmetrically at about ±0.23, with three buttons per player arranged near them, and I'm still sorting out how to fit the start buttons into the centre without them colliding.

I'm now trying to place the joysticks and buttons so the two players don't collide: the sticks sit out near ±0.25, with the buttons inboard of them and the start buttons kept clear at the centre.

I'm placing the joysticks at x ±0.26 with their base plates just inside the cheeks, and spacing the three buttons per player at about 0.05 apart. The start buttons go nearer the back at ±0.03, so the two rows don't collide. Now I'm writing the JSON.

I'm going to write a buildControlDeck function that takes Ctx, making a static model with no joints. I'll use b.part with an "at" position and no bone, so it attaches to the nearest joint or the root. The aim is something compact but still detailed. Still writing the plate geometry...
